name: @deepseek-ai/dsh-api-gateway
description: chamber fork (WP3/M3) of the upstream api-gateway CLIENT half (Typert Remote stream/event carriers) with the per-entry base-path patch: the /api/remote.mux WebSocket lands under the control-plane per-instance proxy prefix (basePath=/api/i/<id>). Host-only deps (dsh-host-webserver; stream-server.ts / index.ts not copied) are intentionally dropped from peer/dev sets; exports map mirrors upstream incl. the inert ./types subpath (its source is a host/aux file, not copied; upstream a4 dropped the ./invariant companion — mirrored). Fork patch 2 (design 14 §D4): a second carrier failure inside a LIVE connection generation is paced and reopened instead of escaping as a terminal gateway/internal error, so the session controller can no longer latch failEventStream() on transport churn. Fork patch 3 (design 14 §D4, 2026-09 ui-chat freeze): the logical-stream opener refuses to send its open frame into a socket that was replaced or is closing (RFC 6455 would discard it silently) and arms an opening-item deadline (30 s, doubling while timeouts stay consecutive, capped at five minutes (30 s → 60 s → 120 s → 240 s → 300 s)) so a lost opening frame re-enters the paced reopen lane instead of hanging the session forever at chat.loadingHistory; RemoteJournalStream arms a silence watchdog that probes a sibling follow and replaces the physical generation only when the Host cursor actually advanced; bounded lifecycle forensics (dsh-chamber:stream-forensics) name every socket and generation transition. Fork patch 4 (design 14 §D4, 2026-09): an opening-item deadline that expires on a socket which delivered NO frame during the whole budget window replaces the physical socket (the same teardown the connection lane's reconnect uses) instead of re-issuing into it — an OPEN-but-silent carrier (an ssh tunnel or direct-http leg whose FIN never arrived) can no longer park a session at chat.loadingHistory with nothing in the page able to see it, and the escalation publishes one bounded socket-silent forensics fact. The same escalation also runs on logical-stream TEARDOWN: a stream that saw no frame on its socket across a life of at least the shared table's SILENT_TEARDOWN_MIN_MS floor (15 s, table-owned) replaces it, which is how the journal watchdog's 20 s sibling-probe abort — earlier than the 30 s budget — still reaches the verdict; a shorter life never judges the socket, because every reconnect starts one whose frame counter is zero.
